newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks end just up,NAB props market.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks end just up,NAB props market.

text.p: SPI futures cl 2438 unch US 30yr cl 6.83 +0.04
10yrbond futs cl 92.580 -0.010 Gold NY 350.75 Lon Fix 350.10
*Stocks ended mixed session just firmer with NAB propping up the market after its Q1 profit result. Volume 454.2 million, value A$838.5 million, 1,096 stocks traded, 331 steady, 376 up, 389 down.

Australian shares ended a point up on Thursday with weaker resources counteracted by a buoyant banking sector which was inspired by sector leader National Australia Bank after it reported strong first quarter earnings.
The key share barometer, the All Ordinaries index, closed one point firmer at 2,434.5. March share price index futures finished steady at 2,438, a 3.5 point premium to the index.

National Australia released its profit figures 15 minutes before the open and its shares climbed steadily from the start of trade, investors reacting favourably to its 18 percent rise in first quarter pre-tax earnings to A$921 million.
"NAB came through with a very good result and consequently banks led the way for the rest of the day," said a dealer from Brisbane firm, Morgan Stockbroking.

The dealer said that action amongst the major issues was subdued but there was plenty of speculative interest amongst small gold explorers with interests in the prospective Gawler Craton region of South Australia.
"The smaller miners are still releasing quarterlies so this is where a lot of investor attention is being focused," he said.
Holding back the market was continued selling of major resource issues BHP and CRA.
Despite interest at the speculative end of the market the gold sector finished weaker after the price of bullion fell to the US$350 level in New York on Wednesday.
Dealers said the direction on Friday would remain strongly linked to the Dow's moves but in the absence of any strong leads the market was likely to continue to drift sideways.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivative trade was quiet with options turnover lifted slightly by interest in National Australia Bank call options following its healthy first quarter report.
Total options traded 34,245 (28,310).
Turnover in March SPI contracts 6,641 (6,741).
In other markets, Australian bonds finished slightly weaker but above key support levels despite a much weaker showing from the Australian dollar.
The yield on 10-year T-bonds closed at 7.33 percent, up 0.01 percentage point from Wednesday's close.
The Australian dollar teetered on the brink of a major downtrend Thursday after sellers far and wide clattered the currency down to 5-1/2 month lows.
By 5.15 pm (0615 GMT) the local dollar had crumpled to US$0.7714/19 from an early US$0.7758/63 and US$0.7768/53 late here Wednesday.
